findings.description: The user_data script embeds a plaintext AWS access key ID and secret access key. These are stored in the instance's user data (also visible in Terraform state and via the EC2 metadata service) and can be trivially extracted by anyone with access to the instance or the API, leading to credential compromise.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the setting is commented out), meaning data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest, risking exposure of sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are shared.

The EBS snapshot has no encrypted attribute set and is explicitly noted as unencrypted, meaning the snapshot data (and any derived volumes) is stored in cleartext, exposing potentially sensitive data if the snapshot is shared or accessed improperly.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the host.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 without any additional restriction, unnecessarily broadening the attack surface for the web service to the entire internet.

The security group permits all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which violates defence-in-depth principles and could facilitate data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet unless carefully controlled elsewhere.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of instances to the internet unless carefully controlled elsewhere.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning flow log data (which can reveal network topology and traffic patterns) is stored unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access control / public exposure hardening
findings.description: The bucket has no associated public access block, versioning, or bucket policy restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, allowing the bucket and its logs to be trivially deleted and leaving no protection against accidental or unauthorized public exposure.
There is no bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport, so data could be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections to the bucket.
